Old Twelfth Night Wassail

Old Twelfth Night Wassail Celebration

Celebrate the Old Twelfth Night Wassail by waking the apple trees and blessing the orchards with traditional songs, noise, and festive foods. This day honors the guardian robin and the hope for a fruitful harvest.

  1. Morning

    Prepare Mulled Cider and Apple Cakes

    Start the day by making hot mulled cider and baking apple cakes to share during the wassailing procession. These warming treats will keep spirits high in the frosty air.

    Recipes: Mulled Cider · Old Twelfth Night Apple Cake

  2. Late Morning

    Gather Ingredients and Supplies

    Collect cider-soaked toast, blue cheese, and pork pies to offer as refreshments between visits to the orchards. Prepare pans and muskets for the traditional noise-making.

    Recipes: Blue Cheese Spread for Old Twelfth Night Wassail · Traditional Pork Pie

  3. Early Afternoon

    Begin Orchard Wassailing

    Visit the apple orchards, banging pans and firing muskets into the branches to wake the trees. Sing traditional wassail songs to encourage a bountiful harvest.

  4. Mid Afternoon

    Offer Cider-Soaked Toast to the Robin

    Place cider-soaked toast in the branches as an offering to the guardian robin, symbolizing protection and good fortune for the orchard.

  5. Late Afternoon

    Share Festive Foods

    Gather with friends and family to enjoy the prepared mulled cider, apple cakes, blue cheese, and pork pies, fueling the continued rounds through the orchards.

    Recipes: Mulled Cider · Old Twelfth Night Apple Cake · Blue Cheese Spread for Old Twelfth Night Wassail · Traditional Pork Pie

  6. Evening

    Reflect and Rest

    Conclude the day by reflecting on the blessings of the orchard and the community spirit fostered through the wassail tradition.

End the day feeling connected to the land and hopeful for a fruitful year ahead.
